html:
Philibert Tsiranana was the first president of Madagascar, leading it from 1959 through independence on 26 June 1960 until he was forced out in 1972.

A teacher from a cattle herding family of the northwest, he came from the coastal peoples rather than the Merina elite of the highlands. He founded the Social Democratic Party and won the trust of France after the uprising of 1947.

His government kept close ties with France, which kept bases and advisers. Discontent with poverty, French influence and his heavy hand grew. In 1972 student and worker protests filled the streets of Antananarivo, and he handed power to the army. A few years later Didier Ratsiraka turned Madagascar socialist.
sum: Philibert Tsiranana was the first president of Madagascar, leading it from 1959 through independence on 26 June 1960 until he was forced out in 1972.
